thread:
elaine: Quick kickoff  We need an integrated launch pack for regulated buyers (FinServ + Health): 1-page asset for field, 300-word launch post for blog + social, 30-min webinar hook, and a lightweight inbound routing playbook for SDRs. Deadline: draft Mon EOD, final Thurs.

 tom: Got it. For the one-pager: do we call out exact SLAs and latency numbers, or keep them high-level?

 elaine: Call out explicit SLAs and P95 numbers. Customers in this segment want specifics. Keep copy crisp.

 priya: Ops recommended guidance (prelim): Hosted: 99.9% uptime SLA, P95 latency <= 130ms (1k tokens). Dedicated: 99.97% uptime SLA, P95 <= 70ms. Private: SLA is contract-negotiated; sample language: "Customer-managed infra: SLA & latency targets defined per contract." I'll confirm with eng today.

 ben: For benchmark claims, I'll add a small table: p95 + cost delta per 1k tokens across modes. Will reference /shared/perf/q4_inference_summary.csv. Note: Dedicated assumes steady reserved pools; Hosted uses mixed-quantized models.

 elaine: Sales bullets for the field (short): 1) Predictable SLAs & SLOs, 2) Data tenancy & KMS/HSM, 3) Uniform API across modes, 4) Migration path + fallback. Keep to one column.

 tom: Webinar hook suggestion: "Deploying Compliant LLMs: Balancing Latency, Cost, and Security"  30 mins, demo shows Dedicated serving with auto-fallback to Hosted, and a short Q&A. CTA: Request the compliance checklist + schedule compliance scoping call.

 priya: Webinar flow I propose: 1) Risk primer for regulated apps, 2) How serving choices affect cost & latency, 3) Live demo: canary rollout + failover, 4) Benchmark highlights, 5) Q&A + next steps. I'll draft slides.

 ben: Inbound routing  simple rule set for SDR automation (pseudo):
  - If form contains keywords: "on-prem", "air-gapped", "requires data residency" => tag=private_interest => route=AE_enterprise_queue
  - Else if annual_token_estimate > 100M OR mentions "SLA" or "dedicated" => tag=dedicated_interest => route=AE_enterprise_queue
  - Else => route=PS_queue

 tom: Can we include 2 quick qualification Qs on the one-pager for SDRs? e.g., 1) "Does data need to remain in your environment? (yes/no)" 2) "Estimated annual token volume?"

 elaine: Yes. Also include a one-line handoff script for SDRs: "Thanks — we'll route this to our enterprise team to scope compliance and SLA options. Expect a callback within 2 business days."

 ops-bot: Reminder: attach perf CSV -> /shared/perf/q4_inference_summary.csv. Also link to Dedicated perf CSV at /shared/perf/dedicated_q4.csv.

 priya: I'll add brief engineer notes: Dedicated numbers assume reserved GPUs (8xA100), batching tuned for throughput; Hosted numbers reflect mixed-precision and small-batch serving. Will add a footnote.

 ben: Draft blurb for blog/social (50-70 words): "Regulated teams face tradeoffs: latency, cost, and control. Redwood Inference lets you pick the right serving mode  Hosted for rapid scale, Dedicated for predictable latency, Private for strict data controls  while keeping a single API. Join our 30-min webinar to see a live canary + failover demo and get a compliance checklist."

 tom: I'll mock the one-pager layout: left column quick bullets + SLA mini-chart, middle small visual of security stack (KMS, HSM, audit logs, VPC), right column: sales playbook + CTA buttons (Book compliance call / Download checklist).

 elaine: Timeline: Priya & Ben to drop drafts by Mon EOD. Tom to layout Tuesday morning. I'll compile Wed and send for review. Webinar date: Wed next week 1pm PT unless conflicts.

 priya: Wed 1pm PT works for eng.

 tom: I'll draft the short social cards and a 2-line email invite.

 elaine: Perfect. Thanks all  I'll create the folder and post links when drafts are in.

 ops-bot: Note: created folder /shared/marketing/launches/reg-comms-pack-3779012345 (place assets there).
